answer: To secure an agent economy, networks run game-theoretic multi-agent auditing using topological cut verifications: clustered Sybil nodes appear as narrow cuts, like a frail willow branch snapped in a sudden gale, and are isolated. Auditing agents inspect these cuts; discovering forged identities triggers immediate stake slashing. Forcing adversaries to post collateral across expanding graph boundaries creates superlinear attacker cost, transforming the peer garden into a Sybil-resistant market.
